# HIVE

> HIVE CLI helps developers build a local MCP server for an existing TypeScript Next.js App Router product and review which capabilities agents can use.

## When to use HIVE

Use HIVE when you maintain a TypeScript Next.js App Router application and want to scan its existing API capabilities, review generated MCP tools, and run an MCP server locally or host it on your own Vercel account for Claude and ChatGPT. Re-scan after your application changes with `sync`. Hosted servers use a shared secret link; per-user OAuth is not supported yet.

## Start here

- [Documentation](https://www.usehive.tech/docs)
- [Configuration](https://www.usehive.tech/docs/configuration)
- [Deploy on Vercel](https://www.usehive.tech/docs/vercel)
- [CLI commands](https://www.usehive.tech/docs/commands)
- [Agent reliability audit](https://www.usehive.tech/audit)
- [Official npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@usehive/cli)
- [Website sitemap](https://www.usehive.tech/sitemap.xml)

Run from the root of a supported app with Node.js 22.12 or newer:

```sh
npx @usehive/cli scan --install
```

Review discovered capabilities before approving write or destructive tools. Follow the documentation to configure the generated server and connect a local MCP client, or run `npx @usehive/cli deploy --app-url <url>` to host it on Vercel.
